title: How This Tiny Startup Built the World’s Safest Bike Helmet
gist: Vancouver startup Pikio's Si Oblik road helmet scored 4.61 on Virginia Tech's STAR ratings, about 32 percent better than the previous best, using independently mounted foam sections to manage rotational impact. It costs $379 and has around 80 parts, and the reviewer says the open question is whether an unknown brand becomes a major helmet maker, a tech supplier, or both.

insights.claim: The US CPSC still judges helmets mainly on direct impacts although research shows rotational twisting of the brain is a key concussion risk, so the industry moved ahead of regulation.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Voluntary ratings, not regulation, are driving helmet innovation.
insights.locator: For decades, researchers judged cycling helmets

insights.claim: Virginia Tech's STAR ratings, launched in 2018, turned helmet safety into a competitive contest: five-star helmets went from 4 of the first 30 to 167 of 272 by 2025, forcing tighter grading.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Independent ratings create a marketable ranking that rewards safety R&D.
insights.locator: Only four of the first 30 helmets

insights.claim: Pikio's Si Oblik scored 4.61 on STAR (lower is better), 2.21 points or about 32 percent below the previous best, Canyon's Deflectr at 6.82, while many top helmets score 7 to 10.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: A large step-change in measured safety gives Pikio a marketing edge and a new bar for rivals.
insights.locator: Sitting comfortably ahead of the competition

insights.claim: Oblik splits the foam into independently mounted sections on flexible connection points, with dual-density foam, so it can deform, deflect and detach to manage both linear and rotational energy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Abram
insights.so_what: Mechanical approach differs from slip-plane systems and may be hard to copy cheaply.
insights.quote: the system is able to deform, deflect, and detach depending on the impact's intensity, location, and direction
insights.locator: Most bike helmets use a thin plastic shell

insights.claim: Competing rotational technologies include MIPS (dominant low-friction layer), MIPS Spherical, 6D's ODS, WaveCel, and Canyon's Release Layer System, each addressing twist differently.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Shows a crowded field of rotation-management technologies competing on STAR scores.
insights.locator: Other helmet technologies approach the problem

insights.claim: Founder Daniel Abram attributes Pikio's first-try result to 18 years in impact research, including BrainShield at Simon Fraser University and BiaGuard, whose IP MIPS bought for about $1 million in 2022.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Deep-domain founders, not newcomers, are behind the leading product.
insights.quote: comes from 18 years researching impact protection and helmet design
insights.locator: How has this relatively obscure Vancouver startup

insights.claim: The reviewer sees Pikio's path as uncertain: MIPS turned an independent technology into a licensed industry standard, and Oblik could follow, making Pikio a brand, a technology supplier, or both.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Licensing could be a bigger business than selling helmets.
insights.locator: For a company most cyclists have never heard of

insights.claim: At $379 the Pikio is $219 more than the Canyon Deflectr RLS because it uses about 80 components versus eight to 10 in a standard helmet.
insights.speaker: Daniel Abram
insights.so_what: Manufacturing complexity makes it a premium niche product and limits volume.
insights.locator: At $379, the Pikio is a premium choice

insights.claim: Pikio offers a 30 percent discount on a replacement for a damaged helmet and has had four helmets returned and replaced so far.
insights.speaker: Daniel Abram
insights.so_what: Crash-return program provides real-world data to validate lab results.
insights.quote: So far we’ve had four helmets returned and replaced
insights.locator: Lab testing is one thing, but real-world data

insights.claim: The reviewer finds the Si Oblik light enough at 279 grams, comfortable, and well-vented with 17 vents after a month of riding, with few compromises.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Suggests safety gains do not come at serious usability cost.
